beats.intro: Chapter sixty. [[sub]]Multiplying and dividing radicals is simpler than adding them: the radicands can join together.
beats.mult: When two radicals have the same index, multiply them under a single radical sign. [[ex]]The square root of five times the square root of seven [[one]]is the square root of five times seven, [[ans]]the square root of thirty-five. [[why]]This is the same rule as before, read the other way: the square root of a times the square root of b is the square root of a b.
beats.coef: Coefficients multiply with coefficients, and radicands with radicands. [[ex]]Seven root eight times two root ten. [[c]]Outside: seven times two is fourteen. [[r]]Inside: eight times ten is eighty. [[mid]]That's fourteen root eighty. [[simp]]Eighty is sixteen times five, so root eighty is four root five, [[ans]]and the answer is fifty-six root five. [[warn]]Keep the coefficients outside. They never go under the radical sign.
beats.div: Division works the same way. [[ex]]Twelve times the fifth root of twenty-one, divided by six times the fifth root of three. [[c]]Outside: twelve divided by six is two. [[r]]Inside: twenty-one divided by three is seven. [[ans]]The result is two times the fifth root of seven. [[same]]The indexes must match: here both are five.
beats.order: With several operations, go left to right. [[ex]]The cube root of eight, divided by the cube root of two, times the cube root of ten. [[s1]]Eight divided by two is four, [[s2]]and four times ten is forty. [[s3]]The cube root of forty simplifies: forty is eight times five, [[ans]]so the answer is two times the cube root of five.
beats.rat: A fraction with a radical in its denominator isn't considered simplified. [[ex]]Take six over root seven. [[idea]]Multiply the top and the bottom by root seven. That's multiplying by one, so the value doesn't change. [[bot]]On the bottom, root seven times root seven is seven: the radical is gone. [[top]]On the top, six root seven. [[ans]]So six over root seven equals six root seven over seven. [[name]]This is called rationalizing the denominator. [[num]]Check with decimals: both are about two point two seven.
beats.rat2: Simplify first when you can. [[ex]]Eight over root twenty. [[s1]]Root twenty is two root five, so this is eight over two root five, [[s2]]which reduces to four over root five. [[s3]]Now multiply the top and the bottom by root five. [[ans]]The result is four root five over five.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]Radicals with the same index multiply and divide under one radical sign. [[w2]]Coefficients stay outside and combine with each other. [[w3]]Simplify the result. [[w4]]To rationalize a denominator, multiply the top and the bottom by the radical in the denominator. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter sixty, and of unit eleven.
